Bowen and Kennedy close on a commitment whose external circumstances remain genuinely unresolved, and the resolution is that both men have stopped treating the uncertainty as a reason to refuse.

entries.name: The Promise Is About This Book
entries.description: The guarantee attaches to the volume in the reader's hand, not to the series it belongs to.

examples.text: Singh advances a decade-long series arc and still resolves the volume's couple completely, which is the standard a series romance is held to.

examples.work: A Court of Thorns and Roses
examples.text: Maas completes a full emotional movement in the first volume before the sequel reopens the question, so the deferral is signalled by a change in the book rather than concealed in the structure.
A second consecutive volume defers the guarantee, and the reader is given no basis for estimating when it will be paid, which converts anticipation into an unpriced debt.

entries.name: The Cost Requirement
entries.description: An ending nobody paid for does not satisfy. Name what each of them gave up.

examples.text: Kinsale's heroine forfeits her religious community and her standing within it, permanently and on the page, which is why the ending reads as a decision rather than a reward.
Tóibín makes the choice a forfeit of an entire second life that the reader has been shown in full, so the cost is quantified before it is paid.
The cost is paid completely and the guarantee is declined, which isolates the point exactly: sacrifice alone does not produce the genre's ending, and a romance owes both.

entries.name: The Choice Requirement
entries.description: The ending must be chosen by the characters, not delivered to them by circumstance.

examples.work: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
examples.text: Sciamma makes both women's decisions explicit and constrained, so what they choose is legible even where the outcome is imposed.
Milan's heroine has the option of safety and takes the exposed position deliberately, which places the decision rather than the danger at the ending's centre.
The premise removes consequence entirely, so the only thing the ending can be made of is a choice, and the film is structured to make that inescapable.

entries.name: The Promise Constrains the External Plot
entries.description: An outside event may endanger the couple; it may not resolve them.

examples.text: Robb settles the relationship's terms independently of the investigation, so catching the killer never doubles as the romantic resolution.
Cole runs the espionage plot to its own conclusion and requires a separate reckoning between the two agents, which keeps the mission from paying the emotional debt.
Roberts resolves a decades-old threat and then gives the couple a further negotiation about how to live, because the danger ending is not the same event as the relationship ending.

entries.name: The Ending's Evidence
entries.description: The promise is a claim about a future the narrative cannot reach, so it must be evidenced rather than asserted.

examples.text: Bujold demonstrates the couple functioning under exactly the social pressure that had made them impossible, which is evidence rather than assurance.
Quinn's epilogue answers the specific fear the black moment raised about the hero's belief that he will die young, rather than supplying general contentment.
The film spends its final act showing the ordinary days the promise consists of, which is the most direct available answer to what happily ever after actually contains.

entries.name: Optimism Is Not Sentimentality
entries.description: The guarantee is a structural commitment; it does not require the book to be soft about anything else.

examples.text: Williams writes addiction, chronic pain and a decades-old abandonment without softening any of it, and still pays the guarantee in full.
The film's final movement is tender and entirely unsentimental, and the optimism is credible precisely because nothing preceding it has been made easier.
Russell keeps both characters' mental illness present through the ending rather than resolving it alongside the romance, which is what stops the optimism reading as a cure.

entries.name: When a Book Declines the Promise
entries.description: It becomes something else, and the something else is worth understanding precisely.

examples.text: Wong builds every component of a romance and withholds the consummation and the ending, producing a film about restraint that could not exist inside the genre.
Miller writes a love story whose ending is fixed by the source myth, so the reader's foreknowledge does the work the genre's guarantee normally does, in reverse.

examples.work: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
examples.text: The film ends on a decision to continue despite documented evidence that the relationship will fail, which is an optimism the genre cannot use because it is not a guarantee of anything.

entries.name: Attention Is the Unit of Attraction
entries.description: Replace every statement that a character is attracted with an act of attention. Narration cannot manufacture what noticing produces instantly.

examples.text: Thomas conveys years of thwarted feeling through the precision with which each party tracks the other's physical condition under duress.
The central relationship is built almost entirely from one man paying sustained attention to a woman who is unconscious for much of the film.
Hero and Hori fall for the versions of each other nobody else is permitted to see, so the entire romance is constructed out of privileged observation.

entries.name: Accurate Perception Reads as Intimacy
entries.description: Give each lead one true and unflattering perception of the other, kept private. Accurate knowledge outperforms described desire.

examples.text: Chase's heroine identifies exactly what the hero is bad at and exactly what he is better at than anyone believes, and the correctness of both readings is the courtship.
Every character diagnoses the others accurately and the accuracy is what makes the triangle unresolvable, since nobody can be persuaded of a flattering version.
Hoang has one lead perceive the other's burnout before she can name it herself, which is the clearest form the rule takes.

entries.name: Proximity Is Engineered, Not Asserted
entries.description: If either party could plausibly avoid the other and does not, the reader stops believing the situation. Build a mechanism.

examples.work: The Wall of Winnipeg and Me
examples.text: Zapata uses an employment contract and then an immigration arrangement, so the two are legally rather than emotionally unable to separate.
Wilder makes the shared space a professional obligation with a career attached, which means leaving costs the protagonist his livelihood.
The premise strands one party in a country she cannot legally leave and makes the other criminally responsible for her, which is proximity with two independent locks.

entries.name: The Competence Display
entries.description: Let each lead be excellent at something in front of the other. Watching competence is the fastest non-physical route to desire.

examples.text: Every romantic advance in the film is transacted through professional expertise, and the attraction tracks respect for it exactly.
Bujold's two officers fall for each other's conduct under command pressure, so the courtship is an assessment of professional character.
Nakamura makes the heroine's growing skill the thing that reorders the hero's perception of her, which inverts the usual direction of the device.

entries.name: The Vulnerability Exchange
entries.description: Disclosure must be reciprocal and staggered. One-sided confession produces a therapist, not a couple.

examples.text: Christina Lauren alternate timelines so that each disclosure in the present is priced against a withheld one in the past.
Haynes makes each admission legally and materially dangerous for the person making it, so the exchange is a transfer of risk rather than of information.
Kizu builds the disclosure across a whole volume and lets it cost the discloser a public breakdown, which prevents confession from functioning as relief.

entries.name: Asymmetry: Who Wants It More
entries.description: Equal desire is inert. Give one party more of it, and let the imbalance move.

examples.text: Wu builds a structure in which every party wants someone who wants someone else, and refuses to equalise any of it.
Charles gives the politically endangered party the greater need and the greater power to end it, so the asymmetry runs in two directions at once.
The film keeps the protagonist's desire unreciprocated to the end and finds its satisfying resolution elsewhere, which demonstrates how much structure the imbalance alone can carry.

entries.name: Physical Register
entries.description: The body reports before the character admits anything. Choose which physical channel your book runs on and stay on it.

examples.text: The entire relationship is conducted through instruction in physical movement, so competence, consent and desire arrive on the same channel.
Kinsale's hero loses language after a stroke, which forces the whole courtship into gesture and touch and makes the constraint the novel's engine.

examples.work: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
examples.text: Sciamma runs the film on looking, and makes the act of being observed the erotic event rather than anything that follows it.

entries.name: The Witness Effect
entries.description: Being accurately seen by one specific person, in a world that sees you wrongly, is the genre's core pleasure. Establish the wrong view first.

examples.text: The film establishes an entire institution misreading the protagonist before the one character who reads her correctly appears.
Rai gives both leads public family roles they perform badly, so private recognition is the only place either is accurately perceived.
Kawahara builds the premise on a hero whose appearance is consistently misread by everyone except one person, which states the rule in its simplest form.

entries.name: Deferral as an Engine
entries.description: Delay generates tension only while the reader believes the reason. Refresh the reason or release the tension.

examples.text: Zapata sustains an extremely long burn by changing the obstacle roughly every quarter, so the delay never rests on a single cause.
The series renews the barrier with a genuine competing relationship and a job change, and its weakest stretches are the ones where the delay has no current reason.
Umino makes the deferral a function of each character's unfinished vocational life, so the waiting is caused by something other than the romance.

entries.name: Compatibility Is Not Chemistry
entries.description: Two people who suit each other have no plot. Design the fit and the friction together, and never let the fit arrive first.

examples.text: Christina Lauren start from certified genetic compatibility and make the entire novel about how little that supplies.
Simsion's hero designs a compatibility instrument and falls for the one person it disqualifies, which is the rule stated as a premise.
The film pairs two obviously compatible assistants and generates its tension entirely from what each is unwilling to want.

entries.name: Chemistry Under Stress
entries.description: Attraction that only appears in calm conditions is decorative. Test it where the characters have no attention to spare.

examples.text: Ilona Andrews establish the attraction during combat and negotiation, so it is legible as an involuntary reading of the other's competence.
The central marriage is written almost entirely in exhausted logistical conversation, and the affection is visible in how the labour is divided.
The romances develop through crisis decisions the player makes under pressure, so approval is registered as a response to conduct rather than to courtship.

entries.name: Conflict Is Incompatible Wants
entries.description: Not incorrect information. Two people who each want something legitimate and mutually exclusive.

examples.text: Thomas gives a separated couple directly opposed legal objectives, so every scene is a negotiation with a stated position on each side.
The central couple's conflict is a budget dispute in which both are professionally correct, and the series refuses to make either position foolish.
Novik's two magic-workers disagree about method in ways that are technically substantive, so the argument survives every increase in affection.

entries.name: Give the Obstacle a Defender
entries.description: An obstacle at least one lead would defend as a virtue is one the reader cannot dismiss.

examples.text: Jenkins makes the heroine's commitment to the Underground Railroad a duty she is right to place above the relationship, so the barrier has moral authority.
Marske's obstacle is an obligation to a family the hero has good reason to protect, which makes his caution a form of decency rather than avoidance.
Each party's loyalty to their own class and dependants is defensible, which is why the series can sustain the conflict across years without villainy.

entries.name: The Obstacle Must Harden
entries.description: As intimacy rises, the barrier must be reinforced rather than repeated. A static obstacle produces the stalled middle.

examples.text: Kleypas escalates the social cost of the association at each step, so the same barrier acquires new enforcement as the relationship advances.
The series attaches an explicit supernatural penalty to intimacy, which converts the obstacle into something that literally worsens on contact.
Black raises the political stakes of the attachment every time either party concedes ground, so each advance costs more than the last.

entries.name: Internal and External Conflict Share a Joint
entries.description: Attach them at one point: the thing that endangers her is the thing she cannot say.

examples.text: Jenkins ties the soldier's duty and the schoolteacher's community standing to the same decision, so neither can move without costing the other.
Stuart makes the operational secret and the emotional secret identical, so a single disclosure would resolve both plots at once and cannot be made.
The mission's survivability and the crew relationships are governed by the same loyalty mechanic, which welds the external and internal arcs at the level of system design.

entries.name: The Lie the Character Believes
entries.description: State it in one sentence. Then make the plot disprove that exact sentence, not a general version of it.

examples.text: Kleypas's heroine believes she is something to be escaped from, and every plot event is calibrated to that specific proposition.
Cochrun's hero believes he is defective rather than unwell, and the novel is careful to disprove only the first of those.
Rowell's protagonist believes she is only interesting as a derivative of someone else, and the romance and the writing plot disprove it in the same movement.

entries.name: Both Parties Must Be Right
entries.description: If one of them is simply wrong, the book is waiting for them to notice. Give both positions a case.

examples.text: Milan's leads have directly opposed legal claims and each has a legitimate grievance, so no reconciliation is available through argument.
Tolstoy grants the abandoned husband a real case, which is what makes the affair a tragedy rather than an escape.
Both characters are recovering from betrayals they contributed to, and the film gives each an accurate diagnosis of the other's evasion.

entries.name: Stakes That Are Not Death
entries.description: Humiliation, loneliness, obligation, the loss of a self-conception. Mortal peril usually substitutes for a stake you have not found yet.

examples.text: Milan builds an entire novel's tension out of a family sauce recipe and a village's economic future, and the stakes never once become physical.
Fujita generates sustained tension from the risk of being known as one's actual self at work, which is a stake with no violent equivalent.
The film's central risk is class embarrassment in front of someone whose opinion the protagonist has never stopped valuing.

entries.name: The Conflict Must Survive the Sex
entries.description: If consummation resolves the obstacle, the obstacle was sexual tension rather than conflict, and the second half has nothing to do.

examples.text: Dare's two leads have incompatible plans for their own futures, and sleeping together makes the incompatibility more urgent rather than less.
Rooney's couple are sexually compatible from the outset and the class and communication problems are entirely untouched by it.
The stated barrier substantially dissolves after consummation, leaving the later conflict to be supplied by an external threat that arrives from outside the couple.

entries.name: Withholding With a Defensible Reason
entries.description: A secret is only an obstacle while keeping it remains the better choice. Re-test that at every act break.

examples.text: Charles gives both men professional reasons to conceal that remain valid long after trust has developed, so disclosure stays genuinely costly.
Orczy's concealment protects a network of other people's lives, which is the strongest form the justification can take.
Information is withheld past the point where any defensible reason survives, so the later plot depends on characters declining to say obvious things.

entries.name: The Argument That Cannot Be Won
entries.description: Write the fight both parties lose. An argument settled on the merits removes the reason either had to change.

examples.text: Milan's leads argue about money and class from positions neither can abandon without abandoning their own history.
Phillips gives her two leads a professional dispute in which each is right about the other's incompetence and wrong about their own.
The series repeatedly stages disagreements where both parties are correct about the risk and incorrect about the other's motive, and resolves them by concession rather than by proof.

entries.name: Conflict That Changes Shape
entries.description: A long book cannot run one obstacle. Replace it before it exhausts, and make the replacement grow out of the first.

examples.text: Gabaldon converts a survival problem into a political one and then into a question about whether history can be altered, each emerging from the last.
Reid moves the obstacle from professional risk to accumulated resentment about who has borne that risk, which is the same problem aged.
Romance arcs shift from personal reticence to institutional obligation as the player's political position changes, so the obstacle transforms with the plot state.

entries.name: When to Let Them Talk
entries.description: The honest conversation is not the enemy of tension. Have it early, and let the real obstacle survive it.

examples.text: Christina Lauren let the deception be discussed openly well before the end, which forces the book to find a better problem and it does.
Wilder resolves the central deception with a single line that refuses to treat it as an obstacle at all, which is the funniest and most decisive version of the move.

The series structure depends on no conversation ever reaching a conclusion, so each disclosure is immediately superseded by another concealment across multiple volumes. It teaches the wrong lesson at scale: that indefinitely deferred communication is a renewable source of tension rather than the exhaustion of a plot that has no obstacle left.

entries.name: What the Black Moment Must Do
entries.description: Force a choice under maximum pressure, between the relationship and the thing each lead has organised their life around.

examples.text: Crusie's black moment turns the town, the family and the law against her heroine simultaneously, and requires her to choose between protecting her sister and keeping the man, with both losses fully specified and neither recoverable. It is the model instance because the pressure is external, the choice is genuinely between two goods, and the reader can see exactly what is forfeited the moment it is forfeited.
Kinsale sets a vow against a life and gives her heroine no third option, so the moment is a decision rather than a misfortune.
McQuiston's crisis requires the protagonist to act in a way that will lose her the other woman if it succeeds, which is the structure at its cleanest.

entries.name: The Black Moment Is a Choice, Not an Event
entries.description: Something happening to the couple is a plot beat. Something one of them decides is the black moment.

examples.text: Cole's crisis is generated by a decision the hero makes about his own nature rather than by an external attack.
Briggs makes the low point a deliberate refusal of protection, which the heroine chooses knowing the cost.
Relationship setbacks arrive as consequences of player decisions rather than as scripted misfortunes, which is the medium's version of the same rule.

entries.name: Placement, and the Third-Act Separation Problem
entries.description: The received wisdom that the couple must break up near the end is the single most damaging piece of advice in circulation.

examples.work: Nine Rules to Break When Romancing a Rake
examples.text: MacLean places the crisis where the heroine's project completes rather than at a prescribed percentage, so the structure follows the book.
Rai keeps the couple in contact through the low point and generates the pressure from a professional exposure instead, which loses nothing.

The two leads are separated for almost the entire film, which is the device taken to its limit and demonstrates the cost: no reckoning between them is possible, so the ending has to substitute recognition for repair.

entries.name: The Separation Is Optional; The Reckoning Is Not
entries.description: What the genre requires is an accounting for harm. Physically parting the couple is one way to stage it, and usually the weakest.

examples.work: A Rogue by Any Other Name
examples.text: MacLean keeps her couple married and in the same house through the crisis, so the reckoning has to be conducted face to face over weeks.
The series stages its most serious relationship crisis without separation, requiring both parties to continue working together while unresolved.
Nakahara's low point is a sustained failure to say the thing, conducted in continuous proximity, which is more painful than absence would be.

entries.name: What Makes a Grovel Land
entries.description: Accurate naming of the specific harm, without qualification, plus evidence the person understands why it was harmful.

examples.text: Heyer's hero has to accept a correction of his self-image from someone with standing to give it, and the concession is specific rather than general.
Ryan requires the apology to name a pattern rather than an incident, which is the version that convinces a reader who has been paying attention.
Heyer's climax forces a comprehensive admission of misjudgement from a character whose competence has been the book's premise, at the maximum cost to his dignity.

entries.name: The Grovel Is Behaviour, Not Speech
entries.description: A speech is a claim. An act that costs the speaker something is evidence.

examples.text: Hoyt's hero makes a public gesture that forfeits reputation rather than money, which is the currency his character actually values.
The apology is enacted through a legal and social intervention with witnesses, so the correction is administered in the same venue as the injury.
Repair is staged as sustained changed conduct over episodes rather than as a scene, which is the most accurate depiction of what repair actually requires.

entries.name: Who Owes the Repair
entries.description: Identify who caused the harm before deciding who apologises. The genre has a long habit of getting this backwards.

examples.text: Jenkins makes the party who concealed his identity carry the entire debt, and does not distribute it to the person who was deceived.
Sebastian keeps the reckoning with the person who reacted badly to a disclosure rather than with the person who made it.

The film's romantic resolution proceeds directly from a sequence in which one boy hands his unconscious girlfriend to another, and neither the plot nor the ending registers a debt of any kind. It teaches the wrong lesson structurally: that an injury committed against a character outside the central couple carries no cost inside it.

entries.name: Forgiveness Must Cost the Forgiver
entries.description: If the wronged party simply resumes, the injury was never real. Show what accepting the apology requires them to give up.

examples.text: Cole's forgiveness requires the surrender of a revenge that has been the character's organising purpose.

examples.work: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
examples.text: Reid makes forgiveness a decision to accept a version of the past the forgiver finds humiliating.
Rowell's protagonist must abandon the belief that she was the wronged party, which is a costlier concession than any apology she receives.

entries.name: The Reversal of the Wound
entries.description: The strongest endings arrange for the other party to do precisely the thing the wound said nobody would do.

examples.text: Charles's hero has been abandoned by everyone with an obligation to him, and the resolution consists of someone with no obligation refusing to leave.
Kingfisher's hero believes himself uncontrollably dangerous, and the ending requires another character to make an informed decision to stay anyway.
Rowell's protagonist expects to be discarded when inconvenient, and the novel's most consequential act is a long drive undertaken specifically to refute it.

entries.name: Repair Without a Grovel
entries.description: When both parties failed, a one-sided apology is a distortion. Write the mutual accounting instead.

examples.text: Cole distributes the failure across both leads and has each name their own contribution rather than the other's.
Reid's oral-history structure lets both parties give incompatible accounts of the same harm, so the repair is an agreement to hold both.
Jalaluddin has the reckoning conducted partly through families and community, which distributes the repair beyond the couple who caused it.

entries.name: A Sex Scene Must Change the Relationship State
entries.description: The rule the whole category rests on. A scene that leaves the couple knowing and owing exactly what they knew and owed before is decoration.

examples.text: Dare's scenes each renegotiate a stated marriage contract, so every encounter alters a term both parties can name.
Hibbert makes each scene expose a widening gap between what her heroine contracted for and what she has started to want.
Ward attaches a physiological consequence to intimacy within his rule system, so the act permanently changes both parties' options.

entries.name: Heat Level Is a Promise
entries.description: Cover, blurb and category have already told the reader what they are getting. Deliver that, at that intensity, at roughly that frequency.

examples.text: Heyer's register is established in the first chapter and never varies, so the reader's expectations are set and met without a single explicit scene.
Kennedy signals a high-heat new-adult contract early and sustains it, which is why the emotional material lands rather than reading as interruption.
Grace's marketing declared an explicit sports romance and the book's distribution of scenes matches the declaration, which is the whole obligation.

entries.name: The Closed Door Is a Technique
entries.description: Not an absence. The break still has to carry a state change, and the constraint redirects the intimacy somewhere else.

examples.text: Lewis's constraint pushes the entire physical register into looks and permitted proximity, which the community's rules make legible as events.
Shiina builds years of intimacy out of hand-holding and standing close, demonstrating that the ceiling determines the vocabulary rather than the intensity.
The film cuts away and puts the significant material in domestic aftermath, which is where its argument about a life together actually lives.

entries.name: What the First Scene Establishes
entries.description: It sets the book's physical grammar and tells the reader what the rest will be made of. Place it where the obstacle is costliest to ignore.

examples.text: Carey uses the first encounter to establish an entire ethical and religious system governing what follows, so the scene is exposition of the highest order.
Bowen's first scene establishes disability, logistics and negotiation together, which sets the terms every later scene works within.
Williams places the first encounter in a shared past, so the present-day scenes are read against an established grammar the reader acquires late.

entries.name: Escalation Is Emotional, Not Explicit
entries.description: Scenes must rise in stakes, not in explicitness. A book that escalates only in detail has nowhere to go by the third one.

examples.text: Singh escalates by increasing what each party is required to reveal about a dangerous ability, not by increasing detail.
Hoang's later scenes are less explicit and more consequential than her earlier ones, because the escalation is in what is being admitted.
Kizu escalates through disclosure of grief rather than of the body, and the physical progression follows the emotional one rather than leading it.

entries.name: Point of View Inside the Scene
entries.description: Stay in one perception. A scene that reports both parties' experience simultaneously has left the body and become choreography.

examples.text: Frost's first-person restriction means the reader learns the other party's state only through what the narrator can observe, which sustains uncertainty.

examples.work: A Court of Thorns and Roses
examples.text: Maas's single first-person POV keeps the scenes inside one nervous system, and the limitation is what makes them read as experience.
Henry keeps the perceptual frame tight enough that the reader registers self-consciousness and distraction, which is what makes the intimacy specific.

entries.name: The Vocabulary Problem
entries.description: English offers clinical, coarse and euphemistic and nothing neutral. Choose one and hold it — the register is a characterisation.

examples.text: Hall picks a plain, slightly wry register that matches his narrator's voice exactly, so the scenes sound like the same person who narrates the rest.
Harris uses a colloquial Southern register that is unmistakably her narrator's, which turns a stylistic constraint into voice.
The euphemistic register of the period obscures what has actually happened to the protagonist, which is a problem of comprehension rather than of taste.

entries.name: Negotiation Before the Act
entries.description: In this genre the conversation beforehand is frequently the more charged scene. Write it as seduction rather than as paperwork.

examples.text: Carey's formal signalling system means every negotiation is conducted in a shared language with real stakes attached to each term.
The game's dialogue structure makes stated preferences a mechanic, so negotiation is literally how the relationship advances.
Rai writes explicit discussion of terms as flirtation, demonstrating that clarity and heat are not in tension.

entries.name: Bodies That Are Specific
entries.description: Generic bodies produce generic scenes. Size, ability, scars, age and unfamiliarity are the material.

examples.text: Blake writes bodies with particular histories and lets unfamiliarity generate both awkwardness and heat.
Takaya makes physical contact conditional on a specific bodily fact, so no touch in the series is ever generic.
Sinclair's partially cybernetic characters have bodies that work differently, and the difference is the scene's actual content.

entries.name: Interruption, Failure and the Scene That Does Not Work
entries.description: Sex that goes wrong is more characterising than sex that goes well, and the genre underuses it badly.

examples.text: Garwood's wedding night fails on both parties' incompatible expectations, which establishes the marriage's actual problem faster than any success could.

examples.work: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
examples.text: Albertalli writes fumbling first intimacy without irony, so the awkwardness reads as tenderness rather than as comedy.
Jeunet builds an entire film around a protagonist who repeatedly cannot complete an approach, and makes the failure the characterisation.

entries.name: Frequency and the Repeated-Scene Failure
entries.description: Three scenes doing one job is one scene printed three times. Count them and give each a distinct function.

examples.text: Roberts spaces encounters at points of decision, so each is attached to something the couple have just settled or refused.
Beverley uses relatively few scenes and makes each mark a change in the pair's legal or social position.
The scenes cluster without individual jobs, so the middle repeats an established position rather than advancing one.

entries.name: Writing Desire Without Sex
entries.description: The most transferable skill in the category, and the one that makes explicit scenes better when you do write them.

examples.text: Wong sustains an entire film on proximity, clothing and the rhythm of a corridor, with nothing consummated and nothing lacking.
Heyer's desire is carried entirely by dialogue and the management of social distance, which is why the restraint never reads as absence.
Oseman conveys want through drawn proximity and hesitation, using a visual grammar prose has to work much harder to reproduce.

entries.name: Consent Is Craft, Not Compliance
entries.description: Treated as a legal box it makes flat scenes. What a person asks for, and how they ask, is characterisation.

examples.text: Dare's negotiations reveal both characters' fears and vanities, so the asking is the most efficient characterisation in the book.
Explicit checking-in is written as warmth rather than as procedure, which demonstrates that clarity has a tone.
Sustained pursuit after clear refusal is framed as devotion, and the narrative rewards persistence in a way the era's convention treated as romantic.

entries.name: Refusal Must Be Genuinely Available
entries.description: Consent means nothing where saying no is not a live option. Engineer the exit and let the character decline to take it.

examples.text: Maxwell builds a political marriage in which one party genuinely cannot refuse, makes that impossibility the novel's central problem rather than its premise, and requires the plot to construct a real exit before the relationship can be believed. It is the clearest demonstration in recent genre fiction that a romance can use a coercive situation as its subject rather than its shortcut, and that the guarantee is only payable once refusal exists.
Bowen gives both parties easy and face-saving routes out of every escalation, so each advance is legible as a choice.
Woodiwiss grounds the captivity in historical conquest, which is more defensible than an invented version, and still leaves the captive without an available refusal at any point.

entries.name: Name the Gradient
entries.description: Where a power difference exists, the book must acknowledge it on the page. An unnamed gradient reads as one the author did not notice.

examples.text: Ashley has the heroine state the imbalance explicitly and set conditions, which is what separates depicting a dynamic from endorsing it.
Lee names the age and fame differentials repeatedly and lets the younger party hold more power than convention would assign.
Ryan writes a controlling relationship and an escape from it with the mechanics of the control made fully explicit.

entries.name: Consent Across Periods
entries.description: Historical settings had different rules and the same bodies. Depict the period's constraint accurately without adopting its position.

examples.text: Dare writes period-accurate social coercion while keeping her heroine's individual agreement explicit and revocable.
Sebastian makes disclosure and consent the same act in a setting where both are dangerous, and stages them as decisions.

Woodiwiss's founding text of the modern historical treats the hero's assault as the beginning of the courtship rather than as an injury requiring reckoning, and the period setting performs no work in the scene beyond removing the heroine's recourse. The structural lesson it teaches is the wrong one: that a historical frame licenses a coercion the book then never has to account for.

entries.name: The Bond That Overrides Choice
entries.description: Fated mating, imprinting and claiming are consent problems by construction. Decide what the bond can override and write the rule down before drafting.

examples.text: Briggs makes pack hierarchy a coercive force her heroine actively resists, so the rule system is an antagonist rather than a shortcut.
Harris gives her narrator a telepathic advantage that partly equalises a supernatural power gap, which is a structural answer to the problem.
The claiming operates over sustained refusal early in the novel and the later relationship is built on top of it without the override being reckoned with.

entries.name: Depicting Coercion Without Endorsing It
entries.description: The book must take a position. There is no neutral depiction, because the ending is an argument about what happened.

examples.text: Sheehan follows the cost of the club's treatment of women across decades and never supplies a resolution that cancels it.
Roberts negotiates the coercion explicitly on the page, which is a real advance on the older convention, and still ends with the captor as the love interest and the structural problem intact.
Wylde is documentary about a subculture's designation of women and declines to take a position, which leaves the reader without one the book has offered.

entries.name: Content Signalling Is the Author's Job
entries.description: Romance has the most developed content-warning culture in commercial fiction and no formal apparatus supporting it. The front matter is a craft surface.

examples.text: Huang's front matter states content plainly and lets readers self-select, which is the current market standard in dark romance.
Grace signals both heat and specific content directly, so the marketing and the book agree.
Score signals a lighter register and a specific set of difficult topics, demonstrating that signalling is not only a dark-romance obligation.

entries.name: Aftermath and Accountability
entries.description: If a scene depicts harm, the book owes the aftermath. Skipping it is the single most common structural failure in the coercive registers.

examples.text: Ryan gives the harmed party an extended recovery with its own arc rather than folding it into the romance's resolution.
Rai lets the consequences of an old betrayal continue to operate after reconciliation, so the repair does not delete the history.
Reid writes accumulated small harms and requires an accounting proportionate to their accumulation rather than to any single incident.

entries.name: The Ending Is an Argument
entries.description: An optimistic ending is a claim about what these people can have, in this world. Know what your ending is asserting.

examples.text: Dunmore's ending argues that a woman can have both the campaign and the man, and constructs the specific legal and financial terms on which that is possible.
Bujold's resolution is an argument about what a society will tolerate, staged in public and settled by political means.
The final movement argues that tenderness remains available after everything the film has depicted, and asserts nothing beyond that.

entries.name: Pay the Guarantee in the Volume
entries.description: The reader bought this book. Whatever the series is doing, this one resolves its couple.

examples.text: Robb settles the relationship's terms in book one and spends the following decades on external plots, which is the model for a continuing couple.
Quinn resolves completely while advancing a family arc, demonstrating that a series arc costs the volume nothing.
The volume closes with the couple separated by the heroine's choice, which defers the guarantee in a book marketed inside the genre's promise.

entries.name: What a Non-Terminal Volume Owes
entries.description: If you defer, the volume still owes a completed emotional movement: a question resolved, a bond confirmed at a new level, a position changed permanently.

examples.text: Gabaldon separates her couple and still completes a full movement about what each is prepared to sacrifice, so the volume settles something.
Ward resolves the volume's couple entirely while leaving the series arc open, which is the interconnected-standalone contract observed.
The volume ends with the relationship's status deliberately unresolved and its terms undisclosed, which works as fantasy and leaves a romance reader unpaid.

entries.name: The Deferred Guarantee
entries.description: Romantasy's convention of one couple across several volumes conflicts with the central promise. Books one to three do not pay it.

examples.text: Novik takes the single-volume settlement, paying the guarantee in full on delivery, which remains the option most romantasy declines without considering.
Kingfisher runs a series in which each volume has its own couple and its own complete resolution, which is the fantasy series that keeps the romance contract intact.

The volume defers the relationship's resolution behind a revelation, and readers arriving through the romance shelf rather than the fantasy one reported it as a broken contract rather than as momentum.

entries.name: Signalling a Deferral Honestly
entries.description: An unsignalled deferral reads as a breach. Signalled, the same structure reads as momentum. The difference is entirely in the front matter and the blurb.

examples.text: Charles establishes a continuing-couple series openly, so readers know from the first volume what each subsequent one will and will not settle.
Marske resolves the volume's couple while flagging the larger arc, which lets the series operate without either promise being ambiguous.
Ilona Andrews signal a slow-burn series romance explicitly, so a first volume that settles almost nothing romantically is read as designed rather than withheld.

entries.name: The Series Couple After the Ending
entries.description: Once a couple's guarantee is paid, it may not be reopened. Development is available; doubt is not.

examples.text: Macomber returns to resolved couples as stable community fixtures who supply resources and advice rather than renewed tension.
Balogh closes a family series without unsettling any of the marriages the earlier volumes established.
The game continues past marriage into an ongoing domestic state with small events and no manufactured crisis, which is the rule implemented as a system.

entries.name: The Last Page
entries.description: The final image is the evidence the reader takes away. Make it specific to the fear the book raised.

examples.text: The closing shot is a choice being made in real time and withholds confirmation, and is complete because both parties know what they are choosing.
Carr closes on the heroine's decision to stay in a place, which answers the exact restlessness the novel opened with.
Miller's final page delivers reunion after death, which is emotionally complete and outside the guarantee, and is the clearest available marker of where the genre's boundary actually runs.

entries.name: Three Taxonomies That Do Not Align
entries.description: Romance is classified three times over, by three parties, and the systems disagree.
entries.principle: A romance novel is simultaneously filed by retailers under subject codes, by publishers under imprint and line, and by readers under trope and heat vocabulary. These systems were built for different purposes — inventory, production and recommendation — and they do not map onto one another. A working writer has to hold all three, because the retailer decides where the book is found, the publisher decides what the book must contain, and the reader community decides whether the book delivered what it promised.
entries.example: A dark mafia romance may carry a single retailer code for Romance/Dark, be acquired by no category line at all because none exists for it, and be discussed by readers in a vocabulary of touch-her-and-die, forced proximity and specific content warnings that appears in neither of the other systems. The same book is three different objects depending on who is describing it.
entries.application: Identify which taxonomy each decision belongs to before you make it. Length and content rules come from the publisher system, discoverability from the retailer system, and expectation management from the reader system — and confusing them produces books that are correctly categorised and unfindable, or findable and mis-sold.

entries.name: The Retailer Taxonomy
entries.description: BISAC subject codes and store categories, built for inventory and now doing marketing work they were not designed for.
entries.principle: BISAC is the North American book trade's subject classification, and its romance section has expanded to absorb distinctions that were previously informal. The current Fiction list carries codes for tropes as well as settings and subgenres, which means the trope layer has become a filing category rather than a critical vocabulary. This is a genuine structural change: a trope is now something a book is registered as, not merely something it does.
entries.example: The romance codes now include Enemies to Lovers, Fake Dating, Friends to Lovers, Second Chances and Love Triangle alongside the older subgenre divisions, so a book declaring one is making a cataloguing statement. Retailer category systems layer further divisions on top for their own storefronts, which is why a title's placement can differ between vendors.
entries.application: Choose your codes as part of the writing decision rather than at upload. A book that half-delivers a coded trope is discoverable by exactly the readers most likely to report it as mis-sold, which is worse than being harder to find.

entries.name: The Publisher-Line Taxonomy
entries.description: Imprints and lines, which classify by production specification rather than by content resemblance.
entries.principle: A publisher's line is a manufacturing category: a set of books produced to a common length, heat level, tone and content specification, on a fixed schedule, for a readership that has been trained to buy the line rather than the author. Two novels in the same line resemble each other in ways that have nothing to do with subgenre, and two novels in the same subgenre may be unpublishable in each other's lines.
entries.example: Harlequin has operated dozens of such lines, each with its own specification — Presents, Desire, Medical, Intrigue, Love Inspired and their historical and suspense variants among them — and a manuscript is assessed against the line's requirements before it is assessed as a novel.
entries.application: If you are writing for a line, obtain its current guidelines and treat them as the specification they are. If you are not, understand the system anyway, because much of what circulates as general romance craft advice is line-specific instruction that has escaped its context.

entries.name: The Reader-Community Taxonomy
entries.description: The vocabulary readers actually use, maintained collectively and answerable to nobody.
entries.principle: Readers classify by trope, heat, configuration, content warning and emotional register, in a vocabulary that evolves continuously and is enforced by review, recommendation thread and shelf tag rather than by any institution. It is the most granular of the three systems and the most responsive, and it is where a book's reputation is actually set. It also carries distinctions the formal systems have no codes for at all.
entries.example: Terms such as why-choose, cinnamon roll hero, touch-her-and-die, third-act breakup and open-door circulate widely as functional categories, and none of them originates with a publisher or a retailer. The shift from reverse harem to why-choose is a community renaming that the formal systems have largely not registered.
entries.application: Read the community vocabulary for your subgenre before writing the blurb, because it is the language your reader will use to decide whether to buy. Use it accurately: adopting a term you have not delivered is the fastest available route to a mis-sold complaint.

entries.name: Holding All Three at Once
entries.description: The practical skill the misalignment demands.
entries.principle: Because no single authority reconciles the three systems, the writer performs the reconciliation. In practice this means making one set of decisions that satisfies a production specification, registers correctly for discovery, and matches the promises the reader vocabulary attaches to those signals. Where the systems conflict, the reader system decides, because it is the one that generates the complaint.
entries.example: A closed-door contemporary in a category line may be coded for retail under a broad romance heading that carries no heat signal at all, while readers filter for heat before anything else — so the cover, blurb and any author's note must carry a signal the other two systems have no field for.
entries.application: Write down, for each book, the line or imprint specification, the subject codes, and the community terms you are claiming. Where a promise exists in only one of the three, make sure it is stated somewhere a reader will see before purchase.

entries.name: What a Category Line Is
entries.description: A continuously published series of short novels produced to a fixed specification, sold as a line rather than as individual titles.
entries.principle: The category line is romance's distinctive publishing structure and has no real equivalent in other genres. Titles are released in monthly slates, formerly numbered, and readers subscribe to or buy the line rather than following authors. This inverts the usual relationship between author and product: the line is the brand, the specification is the promise, and the author's name is a variable within it.
entries.example: Mills & Boon founded in 1908 as a general publisher and turned toward romance in the 1930s; Harlequin founded in 1949 publishing westerns and mysteries, moved to romance exclusively from 1964, and acquired Mills & Boon in 1971. The category system as writers now encounter it grew out of that merger.
entries.application: Understand that writing to a line means writing to a promise you did not make and cannot alter. The compensations are real — a guaranteed readership, a predictable schedule and a working apprenticeship in structure — and the constraint is genuine.

entries.name: The Tip Sheet
entries.description: The document stating what a line requires, forbids and expects, at a level of detail other genres never see in writing.
entries.principle: Lines publish guidance to prospective authors specifying length, tone, heat, setting conventions, point of view and content restrictions. It is the clearest available evidence for this collection's central claim, because the instructions are not about positioning a finished book — they are about what sentences may appear in it. A writer who treats them as marketing preference will produce a manuscript that fails on technical grounds.
entries.example: Love Inspired's published guidance has specified that Christian characters must not drink, gamble or use profanity, and has stated the point-of-view requirement in terms that admit no discretion: hero and heroine only, no secondary-character viewpoint, no first person. That single instruction rules out a large part of the contemporary genre's standard toolkit.
entries.application: Obtain the current sheet before drafting, not before submitting. Guidelines change and old ones circulate for years; a sheet found on a writing forum is a historical document rather than a specification.

entries.name: Word-Count Bands as Specification
entries.description: Length in category romance is decided before the story is, and it determines the story's shape.
entries.principle: Category lines run to defined word-count bands, and the band is not a container but a structural instruction. A shorter band supports one obstacle, one setting and two viewpoints; a longer one supports a secondary cast, a subplot and a second reversal. Writing a single-title structure into a category band produces a book that feels rushed at the end, and the reverse produces a stalled middle.
entries.example: Harlequin's lines have historically run in bands from roughly fifty thousand words upward, with distinct lines occupying distinct bands, and the difference between them is visible in structure rather than in pacing alone. Trade single-title romance typically runs substantially longer and carries the additional apparatus that length permits.
entries.application: Cut your obstacle count to fit the band before outlining. Roughly one substantial obstacle per forty thousand words is a workable starting ratio, and a category-length manuscript with three is a proposal for a longer book.

entries.name: Point of View as a Contract Term
entries.description: Where a line specifies viewpoint, it has specified the reader's access to the story.
entries.principle: Viewpoint requirements are the strongest available demonstration that category guidelines are craft specifications. A line requiring dual hero-and-heroine viewpoint has guaranteed its readers mutual interiority, which removes the possibility of a book built on uncertainty about whether feeling is returned. A line forbidding first person has ruled out an entire contemporary register. Neither restriction is arbitrary; each defines what the line's promise consists of.
entries.example: Love Inspired's requirement for hero and heroine viewpoint only, with no secondary characters and no first person, forecloses the gothic structure, the single-viewpoint suspense structure and the first-person comic voice in one sentence.
entries.application: Check the viewpoint rule before you choose your narrator, because it is the one specification that cannot be fixed in revision. A first-person manuscript cannot be converted to a compliant third-person dual without being rewritten.

entries.name: What a Line Forbids
entries.description: Prohibitions are as load-bearing as requirements, and are more often overlooked.
entries.principle: Line guidance typically states both what a manuscript must contain and what it may not, and the prohibitions are frequently specific about behaviour, content and resolution. They exist because the line's readership has been promised something, and a violation is a breach of that promise rather than a matter of taste. Prohibition lists also encode the line's implicit theology, politics or social model, which a writer should recognise before signing up to reproduce it.
entries.example: Inspirational lines have prohibited depictions of drinking, gambling and profanity by their protagonists; heat ceilings function as prohibitions in the same way, and some lines have restricted how a pregnancy, a divorce or a previous marriage may be resolved.
entries.application: Read the prohibition list first and decide whether you can write inside it honestly. Writing to a line whose restrictions you disagree with produces evasive books, and editors identify evasion quickly.

entries.name: The Numbered Line and the Subscription Economy
entries.description: Sequential numbering, monthly slates and direct subscription built a readership that bought the line rather than the book.
entries.principle: The category system's commercial foundation was reliability of supply: a known number of titles each month, to a known specification, delivered to subscribers or to fixed retail slots. That model produced a vast body of work with unusually stable conventions, and it also produced this genre's specific archival problem — libraries did not accession numbered category titles, so much of the genre's own history is materially difficult to read now.
entries.example: The Dell Candlelight line's numbering is how *Entwined Destinies* is identified today — number 575, published in 1980, by Elsie B. Washington writing as Rosalind Welles — and the number is often the most reliable surviving bibliographic fact about a category title.
entries.application: When researching the genre's history, treat line and number as primary identifiers rather than as trivia. Where a category title cannot be verified, say so; the documentation gap is a fact about the genre and not a failure of your research.

entries.name: Sales Testing, Not Editorial Taste
entries.description: Heat and content levels in category romance have been set by market research for half a century.
entries.principle: The most persistent misconception about category publishing is that its content restrictions reflect editorial conservatism. In practice the lines have been managed as consumer products and their specifications adjusted on measured sales response, which is why heat ceilings have moved repeatedly and in both directions. The specification is an empirical claim about the readership, not a moral position, and it changes when the data does.
entries.example: The industry's mid-century decency conventions gave way after market research demonstrated that more explicit titles outsold sweeter ones — the change was driven by measurement rather than by a shift in editorial conviction.
entries.application: Do not argue with a specification on aesthetic grounds; it is not an aesthetic document. If you want to write outside a line's ceiling, write for a different line or a different structure, and expect the ceilings to move again.

entries.name: The Boom and the Oversupply Collapse
entries.description: The 1980s category expansion ended in a distribution failure, not a collapse in reader appetite.
entries.principle: The category system expanded rapidly through the early 1980s, with many competing lines releasing a large monthly volume into a fixed amount of retail space. The correction that followed was structural: returns rose sharply and lines were cancelled, and the lesson repeatedly misdrawn from it is that readers turned away. They did not. The channel filled.
entries.example: By the middle of the decade the market carried well over a dozen competing lines and a monthly release volume in the dozens of titles, with returns running at a level no publishing category can sustain. Silhouette, launched by Simon & Schuster in 1980, was bought by Harlequin in 1984 in the consolidation that followed.
entries.application: Distinguish channel failure from demand failure when reading any account of a romance category's decline. The distinction matters directly to writers, because a subgenre whose line closed may have a larger readership than one whose line survives.

entries.name: Line Closures and What They Mean
entries.description: A closed line is evidence about retail channels, not about what readers want.
entries.principle: Lines close for reasons that are frequently invisible to readers: shelf space, print economics, subscription decline, corporate consolidation. A trope or setting whose dedicated line has closed often continues to sell strongly elsewhere, which makes line closure a poor guide to what is worth writing. The category system itself has been contracting for years, and the replacements being launched are trade imprints rather than lines.
entries.example: Harlequin closed several lines in 2018, including its western, superromance, inspirational historical, paranormal and Kimani lines; Desire's closure was announced in 2023; the Historical line is scheduled to end after nearly four decades. The Afterglow imprint launched in their place at a substantially longer length and open to multiple subgenres, which is a trade imprint's structure rather than a category line's.
entries.application: Do not read a line closure as a verdict on its content. The clearest case is the western: the dedicated line closed while the cowboy hero remained one of the most reliably selling figures in the indie market.

entries.name: Writing to a Line, in Practice
entries.description: The method, for a writer who wants the apprenticeship.
entries.principle: Category writing is the closest thing the genre has to a formal training system: a fixed specification, fast turnaround, editorial feedback and a readership that will tell you immediately whether the promise was met. The practical method is to read current titles rather than old ones, treat the guidelines as binding, and write to the line's emotional register rather than only to its content rules — which is the part most submissions miss.
entries.example: Many of the genre's most commercially significant authors began in category lines and carried the structural discipline into single-title work, where the habit of one obstacle worked hard remains visible.
entries.application: Read six current titles from the target line before drafting, and identify what all six do in their first chapter. That shared opening move is the line's actual specification, and it is rarely written down anywhere.

entries.name: The Heat Scale as Actually Used
entries.description: An informal, multi-level scale that every part of the market relies on and no institution defines.
entries.principle: Romance operates a working vocabulary of heat levels running from closed-door through to explicit, with further distinctions for frequency, kink and darkness. There is no standard, no governing body and no formal field for it in any retailer system, yet it is the first filter most readers apply. The scale is real, functional and entirely conventional, which means the signal must be carried by cover, blurb, category placement and author's note.
entries.example: Terms such as sweet, closed-door, open-door, steamy, explicit and dark circulate as functional levels with broadly shared meanings, and books are routinely recommended and rejected on them before any other consideration.
entries.application: State your heat level explicitly somewhere a reader sees before purchase, and match it. A mismatch is the single most reliably reported complaint in the genre, in both directions — readers who wanted less are as vocal as readers who wanted more.

entries.name: "Clean" and Why the Word Is Contested
entries.description: A widely used market term that carries an implication many writers and readers reject.
entries.principle: Low-heat romance is variously described as sweet, closed-door, clean or wholesome, and the last two are contested because they imply that explicit content is dirty. The objection is not merely semantic: the terms carry a moral claim into what is otherwise a content-level description, and they map imprecisely onto both the inspirational market and the secular low-heat market, which are different things.
entries.example: Inspirational lines are low-heat because faith content is central; secular low-heat romance is low-heat as a stylistic and audience choice with no religious component. Both are frequently labelled with the same word, which obscures a distinction readers of each actually care about.
entries.application: Prefer closed-door or low-heat for the content description and let the faith content be signalled separately. If you write inspirational romance, say so directly — readers seeking it want the faith element, and readers avoiding it want to know.

entries.name: Closed Door as a Market Position
entries.description: A commercial choice with its own substantial readership, not a limitation.
entries.principle: The closed-door market is large, durable and served by both religious and secular publishing, and it operates on a specific promise: intimacy will be present and will not be depicted. That promise carries craft consequences — the physical register moves to proximity, dialogue and domestic detail — and it carries commercial ones, because the readership includes a significant number of readers who will abandon a book at the first explicit page.
entries.example: Inspirational publishing sustained a closed-door market at scale for decades, and the convention has persisted well outside it in contemporary and historical romance where the reader appeal is stylistic rather than doctrinal.
entries.application: If you are writing closed-door, signal it with equal prominence to an explicit book, because the readership is equally specific. And use the constraint: a closed door redirects intimacy into the material the scene break does not cover, which is where the good writing in this register lives.

entries.name: Explicit as a Category Requirement
entries.description: In several subgenres, explicit content is not permitted but expected, and under-delivering is a breach.
entries.principle: Erotic romance, much of dark romance and substantial parts of the paranormal and sports markets carry an expectation of on-page sex at a stated frequency and intensity. A book positioned in those categories that delivers less is reported as mis-sold in the same way an under-delivered trope is. This is the mirror image of the closed-door promise and is subject to the same rule: the signal creates the obligation.
entries.example: The erotic-romance market was built by publishers operating outside mainstream trade constraints — Black Lace in the United Kingdom from the early 1990s and Ellora's Cave in the United States from 2000 — and established reader expectations about frequency and explicitness that persist in the indie market today.
entries.application: Count your scenes against the expectation of the category you are entering. If the count is low, either raise it, redirect the positioning, or state the difference plainly in the description.

entries.name: Dark Romance and the Signalling Gap
entries.description: The genre's most content-sensitive category has almost no formal signalling apparatus.
entries.principle: Dark romance depicts coercion, violence and captivity as a matter of category definition, and the formal systems recognise it with a single broad code and nothing finer. Every meaningful distinction — what kind of violence, whether consent is negotiated, whether the harm is reckoned with — is carried by author-supplied warnings and community-maintained lists. That gap places the entire signalling burden on the writer, and it is a craft obligation rather than an administrative one.
entries.example: Content-warning practice in the category is entirely conventional: front-matter lists, author's notes and reader-maintained databases do the work that no retailer field performs, and the conventions vary between authors.
entries.application: Write a specific content note rather than a general one, and put it where it will be seen before purchase as well as in the front matter. Specificity protects the book: a reader who was warned and chose it is a reader who wanted it.

entries.name: Who Enforces the Signal
entries.description: Not publishers, not retailers, and since 2024 not any professional body.
entries.principle: Enforcement of the genre's promises is now almost entirely a reader function, exercised through reviews, recommendation networks and return behaviour. The Romance Writers of America wrote the genre's working definition and filed for Chapter 11 in May 2024, with the plan confirmed that July and the case terminated by final decree in November, having lost the large majority of its membership. It continues to operate in reduced form and no successor body of comparable scope emerged. The practical consequence is that the central promise is maintained by readers and retailers rather than by any institution.
entries.example: The awards apparatus illustrates the discontinuity precisely: the RITA ran from 1990 to 2019 and was retired; the Vivian that replaced it was announced in 2020 and awarded once, for 2021; the Diamond Heart is the body's current published-book award, with a first cycle in 2025–26. Guidance describing the Vivian as an ongoing award is stale rather than wrong.
entries.application: Do not rely on institutional definitions of the genre's requirements, because the institution that wrote them no longer performs that function. Rely on the reader system, which is where the promise is now actually held and enforced.

entries.name: What Single-Title Means
entries.description: A romance sold on its own terms rather than as an instalment of a line.
entries.principle: Single-title romance is acquired, positioned and sold as an individual book, which changes almost everything about its construction: it runs longer, carries a secondary cast and a subplot, is marketed on the author's name rather than the line's, and must generate its own readership rather than inheriting one. The freedom is real and so is the exposure — a single title that does not find readers has no line behind it to carry the loss.
entries.example: The genre's major commercial careers of the 1990s and after were built in single title, where authors who had trained in category could work at greater length with a secondary cast and a continuing world of their own rather than the publisher's.
entries.application: If you move from category to single title, expect the extra length to demand a second structural element rather than a longer version of the first. The commonest failure in that transition is a category plot padded to trade length, which produces the stalled middle.

entries.name: The Trade Market and Its Different Promise
entries.description: General trade publishing sells romance to a wider readership on partly different terms.
entries.principle: Trade romance is positioned for bookstore and general-media discovery rather than for genre-channel discovery, which shifts what the package emphasises: voice, premise and cover design over line, heat and trope. The genre's guarantee still applies, but it is signalled less explicitly, which produces a recurring problem — readers arriving through the general channel may not know the promise exists, and readers arriving through the genre channel may not be able to tell whether it is being made.
entries.example: The illustrated-cover trade contemporary of the late 2010s and 2020s deliberately signalled to a general readership rather than to a genre one, and drew sustained criticism from within romance for obscuring heat level and, in some cases, whether a book was a romance at all.
entries.application: If your book is positioned for trade, carry the genre signal in the copy even where the design does not. A reader who cannot determine the heat level or the ending's shape from the description will supply their own assumption, and will report the book against it.

entries.name: Advances, Print Runs and Lead Titles
entries.description: The commercial machinery that decides which books are given a chance to succeed.
entries.principle: Trade publishing concentrates its marketing on a small number of lead titles per season, and a book's print run, placement and publicity are largely determined before publication rather than by early sales. This has a specific consequence for romance: because the genre's readership is channel-driven rather than review-driven, a romance that is not given genre-channel support can perform poorly for reasons unrelated to the book.
entries.example: The genre's own history supplies the clearest evidence of what channel decisions do — the Black romance imprints of the 1990s were commercially viable and were nevertheless subject to distribution and placement decisions that did not match their readership, a pattern documented at length by writers working in the category at the time.
entries.application: Ask about positioning and channel, not only about advance. A larger advance without genre-channel support is a worse commercial position than a smaller one with it, and the distinction is legible before you sign.

entries.name: The Crossover Book
entries.description: A romance that reaches beyond the genre readership, and what that costs inside it.
entries.principle: Books that break out to a general audience typically do so by de-emphasising genre markers, and the genre readership notices. The recurring pattern is that a crossover title is celebrated outside romance for transcending it, on terms most romance readers reject, while being assessed inside romance against the promise it may or may not have made. Both readerships are reading a different object.
entries.example: The pattern is old and consistent: commercially enormous romance-adjacent titles are routinely described in general coverage as exceptions to a genre they belong to, and the framing has been a documented grievance within the field for decades.
entries.application: Decide which readership you are writing for and signal accordingly, because you cannot fully signal to both. If you want the crossover position, be honest in the copy about whether the genre's guarantee is being made, since the alternative is a mis-sold complaint from the readership most likely to buy your next book.

entries.name: Kindle Unlimited and the Page-Read Economy
entries.description: A subscription channel that pays by pages read, which changes what a book is optimised for.
entries.principle: A large share of the current romance market is read through subscription, where revenue accrues per page consumed rather than per copy sold. That single mechanic pushes toward longer books, series that carry readers forward, front-loaded hooks and exclusivity, because the channel rewards continued reading rather than the purchase decision. It also makes reader-behaviour data available to authors at a granularity trade publishing does not supply.
entries.example: Series-first publishing, rapid release schedules and the practice of ending volumes on hooks are all channel-shaped behaviours rather than aesthetic developments, and they are strongest precisely where subscription reading is strongest.
entries.application: Understand which incentive you are writing under before adopting its conventions. A hook ending is a channel-rational choice and a genre-contract risk, and the two considerations must be weighed against each other rather than assumed to agree.

entries.name: Release Cadence as a Craft Constraint
entries.description: Publication rhythm in the indie market is fast enough to determine what can be written.
entries.principle: Visibility in algorithmic storefronts decays quickly, so indie romance has converged on short intervals between releases. That cadence is a genuine craft constraint: it favours series with established worlds, shorter books, familiar structures and trope-forward premises, and it disfavours long research, structural experiment and books that need time. It is neither a failing nor a virtue — it is the shape the channel imposes.
entries.example: Release intervals measured in weeks or a few months are common practice among full-time indie romance authors, and the corresponding structural habits — reusable settings, established casts, declared tropes — follow directly.
entries.application: Choose your cadence before your project, and match the project to it. A book requiring substantial historical research or an unusual structure is not a failure of discipline; it is a book for a different publication rhythm.

entries.name: Series-First
entries.description: Standalones underperform in the indie channel, and the reason is structural.
entries.principle: In a market where discovery is expensive and reading is subscription-based, the economics reward a reader who finishes one book and immediately starts another by the same author. A series supplies that; a standalone does not. The result is that the interconnected-standalone model — each volume its own couple and its own complete promise, in a shared world — has become the market's default structure, and it is well suited to the genre's contract.
entries.example: Small-town, sports, motorcycle-club and paranormal romance are all dominated by interconnected series with returning casts, and the model's compatibility with the genre's per-volume guarantee is why it has held.
entries.application: Plan the container before the first book: what institution, town, team or family will generate the subsequent couples. Retrofitting a series onto a standalone is possible and produces the seams readers notice in book two.

entries.name: Trope-Forward Marketing
entries.description: The tropes are declared before the book is written, and the declaration is a specification.
entries.principle: Indie romance sells on itemised trope lists, and the standard practice is to fix them before drafting rather than to derive them afterwards. This inverts the usual relationship between book and copy, and it has a real craft benefit: a premise that cannot produce a clean trope-forward description usually has an unclear obstacle rather than a marketing problem. It also creates a hard obligation, since a declared trope is a contract term.
entries.example: The formalisation is now visible in the subject-code system itself, which carries codes for individual tropes, so a declaration made in marketing copy is also a cataloguing statement.
entries.application: Write the description first, list the tropes it promises, and check each against the draft at the end. Deliver every declared trope at full strength before you subvert any of them.

entries.name: Covers as Subgenre Signalling
entries.description: Cover design in romance is a category signal before it is an aesthetic choice.
entries.principle: Romance covers communicate subgenre, heat level and register at a glance, using conventions that shift every few years and that readers parse fluently. A cover that departs from its category's current visual language is not distinctive; it is illegible, and the book is filtered out before the description is read. This is the most consequential piece of packaging in the genre and it is frequently the one an author has least control over.
entries.example: The illustrated cover's rapid adoption across contemporary romance in the late 2010s, and the readership's complaint that it obscured heat level, is the clearest recent demonstration that cover convention carries content information the formal systems do not.
entries.application: Study current covers in your exact subgenre, not romance generally, and match the signal. If you must depart from convention, compensate in the description, because you have removed a signal readers rely on.

entries.name: Rapid Release and the Quality Question
entries.description: The argument the market has with itself, stated fairly.
entries.principle: Fast publication is regularly criticised as incompatible with quality and defended as a professional discipline, and both positions have evidence. The honest description is that cadence changes what kind of quality is achievable: it rewards fluency, structural competence and voice, and penalises research depth and structural revision. A writer choosing the model should know which of their strengths it is buying and which it is spending.
entries.example: The category-line system imposed a comparable discipline for decades and produced both a large body of competent formula work and a substantial number of the genre's most structurally accomplished authors, which suggests cadence is a filter rather than a ceiling.
