entries.text: Two distinct classes of Cannes award, frequently reported as one, and a César win that a widely used summary records as a nomination. It received no Academy recognition because France submitted a different film, which is a selection decision rather than a snub. The film runs on looking, and makes the act of being observed the erotic event rather than anything that follows it — the charged non-touch sustained across a whole feature, and the strongest demonstration in the collection that a physical register can be chosen and held.

entries.name: Pride and Prejudice (1995 tv)
entries.author: Simon Langton
entries.awards: BAFTA Television Award for Best Actress, Jennifer Ehle; Primetime Emmy for Costume Design; Peabody Award
entries.description: Adapted by Andrew Davies. Disambiguated from the 1813 novel carded at `work-2` under the pack's shared-namespace rule. Colin Firth was **nominated and…
entries.text: Adapted by Andrew Davies. Disambiguated from the 1813 novel carded at `work-2` under the pack's shared-namespace rule. Colin Firth was **nominated and lost** at the BAFTAs, and the serial won no Best Drama Serial award — both are commonly asserted. Its craft interest against the 2005 film is that it withholds the kiss almost entirely and puts the charge into the second proposal, which demonstrates that the kiss is optional when the acknowledgement is not.

entries.name: Bridgerton
entries.author: Chris Van Dusen
entries.awards: First season, **twelve nominations and one Primetime Emmy win**, for hairstyling
entries.description: Created and showrun by Van Dusen for its first two seasons; its best-known executive producer did **not** create it. The single-win record is worth…
entries.text: Created and showrun by Van Dusen for its first two seasons; its best-known executive producer did **not** create it. The single-win record is worth stating because circulating figures of five Emmys either pool later seasons or count one award across its several credited artists. The series makes the ballroom's surveillance its actual engine, so any public contact is simultaneously an act and a legal event — and its colour-conscious casting became the most-discussed adaptation decision of its decade.

entries.name: Outlander (2014 tv)
entries.author: Ronald D. Moore
entries.awards: **No Emmy or Golden Globe wins** — nominations only; its wins are audience-voted
entries.description: Developed for television by Moore, and disambiguated from the 1991 novel at `work-45`. The award record is frequently overstated: the series has been…
entries.text: Developed for television by Moore, and disambiguated from the 1991 novel at `work-45`. The award record is frequently overstated: the series has been nominated at the major academies and has won at the popular-vote ceremonies, which are different things. The adaptation's contribution is that it stages intimacy under the observation of a household and a clan, converting privacy into a resource the couple must obtain — and it declined to strip the romance out of a romance-centred saga, which comparable prestige adaptations had routinely done.

entries.name: Poldark
entries.author: Edward Bazalgette and others
entries.awards: BAFTA **Radio Times Audience Award**, 2016 — a **public vote**, not a juried BAFTA
entries.description: Adapted by Debbie Horsfield from Winston Graham's novels. The award distinction is the card's reason for existing in the award-record sense: a BAFTA…
entries.text: Adapted by Debbie Horsfield from Winston Graham's novels. The award distinction is the card's reason for existing in the award-record sense: a BAFTA won by public vote is reported identically to a juried one in most summaries. The series' romance interest is that each party's loyalty to their own class and dependants is defensible, which lets the central conflict run for years without anyone becoming a villain — an obstacle with a defender, sustained at length.

entries.name: Jane the Virgin
entries.author: Jennie Snyder Urman
entries.awards: Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy Series, 2015; Peabody Award, 2015
entries.description: The telenovela form brought into English-language network television with its machinery visible. The series gives its gossip economy an on-screen…
entries.text: The telenovela form brought into English-language network television with its machinery visible. The series gives its gossip economy an on-screen narrator, which externalises the mechanism and lets the show comment on its own conventions — including on what its audience is demanding of it. It is the clearest instance in the collection of a romance structure that is simultaneously sincere and analytical about being a romance structure, which is a difficult register to hold across five seasons.

entries.name: Schitt's Creek
entries.author: Daniel Levy and Eugene Levy
entries.awards: **Swept all seven major comedy categories in a single night, 2020** — the first series ever to do so — from fifteen nominations
entries.description: The sweep is the record; totals including the craft awards circulate in several forms and are not stated here. The series takes two full seasons over…
entries.text: The sweep is the record; totals including the craft awards circulate in several forms and are not stated here. The series takes two full seasons over its central romance and makes the delay a function of one character's unfamiliarity with being treated well, which is a reason rather than a device. Its found family is the town itself, and the romance's progress is measured by the couple's willingness to be known by it — the pack's model for a queer relationship written with no homophobia as an obstacle and nothing lost by its absence.

entries.name: Normal People
entries.author: Lenny Abrahamson and Hettie Macdonald
entries.awards: BAFTA Television Award for Leading Actor, Paul Mescal
entries.description: Two directors, splitting the series in half, and a screenplay **co-written** by Sally Rooney with Alice Birch and Mark O'Rowe — sole-author framings…
entries.text: Two directors, splitting the series in half, and a screenplay **co-written** by Sally Rooney with Alice Birch and Mark O'Rowe — sole-author framings are common and wrong. Daisy Edgar-Jones was not nominated. The adaptation stages long stretches of near-contact in ordinary rooms, using duration rather than staging to make the withholding legible, which is the charged non-touch translated into a medium that has to fill the time.

entries.name: Crash Landing on You
entries.author: Lee Jeong-hyo
entries.awards: **One** competitive Baeksang Arts Award — Best Supporting Actress
entries.description: Written by Park Ji-eun. The award record is the inverse of the usual claim: its two leads won **no** Baeksang acting prize for it, and the top drama…
entries.text: Written by Park Ji-eun. The award record is the inverse of the usual claim: its two leads won **no** Baeksang acting prize for it, and the top drama honours that year went elsewhere. Other trophies attached to it are sponsor and popular-vote categories. The premise is the pack's most efficient proximity engine — one party stranded in a country she cannot legally leave, the other criminally responsible for her, which is proximity with two independent locks and no negotiable exit.

entries.name: Virgin River (2019 tv)
entries.author: Sue Tenney
entries.awards: Regional industry awards only — no national or academy award
entries.description: Adapted from Robyn Carr's novels and disambiguated from the 2007 novel at `work-64`. The card is here for what the adaptation demonstrates about the…
entries.text: Adapted from Robyn Carr's novels and disambiguated from the 2007 novel at `work-64`. The card is here for what the adaptation demonstrates about the small-town model rather than for its awards: a community engine with a functioning local economy transfers to television almost without modification, because the structure was always generating episodes rather than chapters. Its longevity is the argument that the community, not the couple, is the durable asset in that subgenre.

entries.name: Heartstopper (2022 tv)
entries.author: Euros Lyn
entries.awards: **Five wins from nine nominations at the first Children's and Family Emmy Awards, 2022** — a different academy from the Primetime Emmys, at which it has no recognition; a BAFTA **nomination** in a public-vote category
entries.description: Created and written for television by Alice Oseman, adapting their own webcomic, and every episode is theirs. The academy distinction matters because…
entries.text: Created and written for television by Alice Oseman, adapting their own webcomic, and every episode is theirs. The academy distinction matters because "Emmy-winning" reads as Primetime by default. The series escalates through disclosure to families, schools and mental health rather than through physical progression, and it is the pack's reference instance for repair staged as sustained changed conduct across episodes rather than as a single scene.

entries.name: Nana
entries.author: Ai Yazawa
entries.awards: **Shogakukan Manga Award, shōjo category** — note that both major manga awards accept works from rival publishers, so a cross-publisher win is normal rather than an error
entries.description: Serialised in Cookie by Shueisha. **On indefinite hiatus since 2009**, and the language matters: the publisher stated only that this followed a sudden…
entries.text: Serialised in Cookie by Shueisha. **On indefinite hiatus since 2009**, and the language matters: the publisher stated only that this followed a sudden illness and **never named a diagnosis**, so every specific illness in circulation is speculation. Yazawa said in 2022 that she still could not restart it. Four chapters remain uncollected. It is neither cancelled nor ended. The work treats sex as the point at which two characters' incompatible plans for their own lives become visible to each other, and refuses to discredit either claim in its central triangle across hundreds of chapters.

entries.name: Fruits Basket
entries.author: Natsuki Takaya
entries.awards: **Kodansha Manga Award, shōjo category, 2001**
entries.description: Serialised in Hana to Yume by Hakusensha, and among the best-selling shōjo manga ever published. The award is a cross-publisher win and is correct as…
entries.text: Serialised in Hana to Yume by Hakusensha, and among the best-selling shōjo manga ever published. The award is a cross-publisher win and is correct as stated. Its structural device is a rule system that makes ordinary physical contact transformative and therefore consequential, so the approach carries weight before anyone has decided anything — the strongest demonstration in the collection that a supernatural constraint can do the work a social constraint does in a historical setting.

entries.name: Boys Over Flowers
entries.author: Yoko Kamio
entries.awards: **Shogakukan Manga Award, shōjo category, 1996**
entries.description: Serialised in Margaret by Shueisha from October 1992; its end date is given inconsistently across sources. One of the most adapted romance properties…
entries.text: Serialised in Margaret by Shueisha from October 1992; its end date is given inconsistently across sources. One of the most adapted romance properties in any medium, with screen versions across several countries. The card also carries a `weak` reading in the Tropes collection: sustained pursuit after clear refusal is framed as devotion and the narrative rewards persistence, which is the era's convention operating at full strength and is why the work is as instructive about what changed as about what it did.

entries.name: Kimi ni Todoke
entries.author: Karuho Shiina
entries.awards: **Kodansha Manga Award, shōjo category, 2008**; a **nomination** for the first Manga Taishō the same year, which it did not win
entries.description: Serialised in Bessatsu Margaret by Shueisha. The series extends the almost-kiss across volumes and makes each near-miss a genuine misreading of the…
entries.text: Serialised in Bessatsu Margaret by Shueisha. The series extends the almost-kiss across volumes and makes each near-miss a genuine misreading of the other's position rather than a contrived interruption — which is the shojo tradition's characteristic refinement of a device that prose romance usually spends once. It is the pack's model for deferral sustained by renewed reason rather than by obstruction.

entries.name: Stardew Valley
entries.author: Eric Barone
entries.awards: None of the major industry awards
entries.description: Developed by Barone alone and **published at launch by Chucklefish** — not self-published, which is how it is almost always described; Barone took…
entries.text: Developed by Barone alone and **published at launch by Chucklefish** — not self-published, which is how it is almost always described; Barone took publishing duties back from late 2018, with the transfer completing in 2022. Romance is a genuine mechanic: courtship proceeds through repeated small gifts and conversations, and the game continues past marriage into an ongoing domestic state with its own events. That continuation is a medium-native answer to the question the pack's Endings section asks — what the guarantee actually consists of once it has been paid — and prose has no direct equivalent.

entries.name: Dream Daddy
entries.author: Game Grumps
entries.awards: **None** — no major industry award
entries.description: A dating simulator in which stated preferences and explicit checking-in are mechanics rather than dialogue flavour, so negotiation is literally how a…
entries.text: A dating simulator in which stated preferences and explicit checking-in are mechanics rather than dialogue flavour, so negotiation is literally how a relationship advances. That is the card's reason for inclusion: the pack argues throughout that consent is craft rather than compliance, and this is the clearest case of a work in which the argument is built into the system. Its award record is empty and its critical reception was mixed, both of which the card states rather than inflating a niche title into a landmark.

entries.name: Baldur's Gate 3
entries.author: Larian Studios
entries.awards: **Six wins at The Game Awards, 2023**, including Game of the Year
entries.description: The romance system's craft interest is that approval is registered as a response to conduct rather than to courtship: the relationships develop through…
entries.text: The romance system's craft interest is that approval is registered as a response to conduct rather than to courtship: the relationships develop through crisis decisions made under pressure, so attraction is legible as an assessment of how the player behaves when it costs something. That is chemistry under stress implemented as a system. The number of romanceable characters circulates as a community tally rather than a developer figure and is not stated here.

entries.name: A Natural History of the Romance Novel
entries.author: Pamela Regis
entries.awards: None
entries.description: Published by the University of Pennsylvania Press. The first sustained argument that romance is a form with a history rather than a product with a…
entries.text: Published by the University of Pennsylvania Press. The first sustained argument that romance is a form with a history rather than a product with a market, defining the genre by the courtship and its ending and identifying eight recurring narrative elements across four centuries. **The book itself states that the elements may occur in any order, be doubled or tripled, and co-occur in a single scene** — and a decade later Regis wrote that she would likely relabel them pragmatic rather than essential. Publishing them as an ordered beat sheet is the standard error, and it is made against the text rather than in the absence of it.

entries.name: Reading the Romance
entries.author: Janice Radway
entries.awards: None
entries.description: Published by the University of North Carolina Press. The first sustained empirical study of a romance readership, and field-defining for treating…
entries.text: Published by the University of North Carolina Press. The first sustained empirical study of a romance readership, and field-defining for treating readers as informants rather than as symptoms. Its edition history is frequently reported wrongly: a self-critical introduction was written for a **1987 British edition** and reprinted in the 1991 American revised edition, and a **second, sharper one is new to the 2009 edition** — two texts from two publishers, and neither is a recantation. Cite the book for its method and its questions rather than for conclusions the author has twice reframed.

entries.name: Romance Fiction: A Guide to the Genre
entries.author: Kristin Ramsdell
entries.awards: None
entries.description: Published by Libraries Unlimited, with a second edition in 2012. The standard readers'-advisory reference for romance, and the work that made the genre…
entries.text: Published by Libraries Unlimited, with a second edition in 2012. The standard readers'-advisory reference for romance, and the work that made the genre navigable for librarians at a point when no institution was describing it systematically — bibliographic classification as a form of advocacy. A citation caution: the 1999 book is itself a rewrite of the author's earlier 1987 guide under a different title, so some catalogues describe 1999 as the second edition and 2012 as the third. Specify the title as well as the year. Her forename is **Kristin**, and the misspelling is widespread enough that it reached this pack's own verification brief before being caught.
